readers.summary: FALSE FLAG is a strictly turn-quantized, LLM-adjudicated crisis sim: each turn runs briefing (YAML or LLM-generated inject applied to metrics) -> free-form advisor discussion -> free-text decision with LLM interpretation/pushback preview -> LLM adjudication (quality assessment, metric deltas, 5-country actor simulation, situation-summary fold, event ledger), then turn+=1 and the engine goes completely quiescent until the client POSTs the next briefing — nothing runs between turns. World state is three 0-100 gauges plus casualties, boolean flags, per-country trust scores, a hidden narrative truth, and a rolling prose summary; the only "spatial" field (WorldState.spatial_state, location-name -> unit-ID lists) is confirmed dead by the repo's own audit — never written, never read. Geography exists as real UK/Russia place-name strings in initial_conditions.yaml (Portsmouth, Faslane, RAF Marham, Orkney, GIUK gap, Severomorsk), in inject prose ("12 nm off Orkney", Drax, RAF Fylingdales), and as three hardcoded DMS coordinate strings for intro scene cards — there are zero machine-readable coordinates anywhere in state, injects, or prompts. The cleanest attachment for a continuous ambient/globe layer is the API tier, not the engine: every session has a layer-tagged SSE event bus (GameSession.push_event, 6-layer enum, t_plus_s wall-clock + event_seq stamps), a facilitator inject endpoint that mutates state through the same primitives as scripted injects, and a proven daemon-thread driver pattern (api/demo.py) that paces beats under session.lock — an ambient GEOINT simulator can stream stream-only events continuously and only touch engine state via deliver_inject at chosen moments, leaving determinism (seeded RNG, RNG-state-carrying saves) intact.
facts: Turn phases are a Literal type: briefing/discussion/decision/adjudication — models/world.py:15; phase is stored on WorldState (models/world.py:23) and reset to 'briefing' after each adjudication (engine/game_manager.py:591).

Turn lifecycle (headless/API path): GameManager.get_turn_briefing loads/generates the inject, applies effects, opens any mandatory diplomatic call, then forces phase='discussion' (engine/game_manager.py:182-258); interpret_decision previews interpretation+pushback+critical-omissions without committing (engine/game_manager.py:367-425); resolve_decision runs the full decision pipeline, syncs hidden_metrics back over world.metrics, checks endings, then world.turn += 1 and phase='briefing' (engine/game_manager.py:506-614, turn advance at :590-592).

Between turns NOTHING executes: after resolve_decision returns, no timers, threads, or schedulers run; the next turn starts only when the client calls POST /game/{session_id}/briefing (api/server.py:872-916). The CLI equivalent is the same synchronous loop (engine/sim_loop.py:793-842).

Injects are single-YAML-dict episode files data/scenarios/{id}/episodes/turn_NNN.yaml loaded by engine/events.py:43-81; fields: id, title, description (prose block), channel, effects [{metric, delta}], optional image, optional diplomatic_encounter {required, country, context} (e.g. turn_006.yaml:29).

Inject effect deltas may be ints, floats, or 'min..max' range strings (midpoint taken); scenario effects are scaled by difficulty multiplier 0.5/0.7/1.0 (standard/challenging/brutal) with a minimum magnitude of 1 — engine/sim_loop.py:188-295 (multipliers :207-212, range parsing :236-250).

Stochastic injects: when the scripted file is missing and turn >= stochastic_from (7 for standard variant, scenarios.yaml:31), the LLM generates an inject in the same YAML shape — prompt mandates only id/title/description/channel/effects, channel from briefing/intelligence/media/military; NO location field exists in the schema (llm/prompts.py:454-468, llm/inject_generator.py:37-138). Failure falls back to a diegetic 'quiet turn' inject (engine/sim_loop.py:38-55).

Standard campaign = 6 scripted turns + stochastic from turn 7 + 4 epilogue turns, then graded; threshold endings (war/collapse/isolation/resolution/uneasy_peace) can fire any turn — data/scenarios/war_game_2025/scenarios.yaml:24-40, engine/endings.py:19,36-80, engine/game_manager.py:473-492.

Metrics: escalation_risk, domestic_stability, alliance_cohesion (0-100) plus casualties_civ/mil counters — models/world.py:6-11. NarrativeState keeps a hidden copy (hidden_metrics) that is authoritative: adjudication mutates hidden_metrics and copies them back over world.metrics, so any effect applied only to world.metrics is silently reverted (documented trap, engine/game_manager.py:236-247, 296-307, 569-573).

WorldState.spatial_state: Dict[str, List[str]] 'location names -> unit IDs' exists (models/world.py:40) but is DEAD — the repo's own LLM-context audit states it is the only occurrence repo-wide, never written, never read, and 'geography exists nowhere in the prompt layer. The 8 UK sites, 3 operational areas and 1 Russian location are unused' (audits/2026-08-05-llm-context/data/agent-reports/synthesis.md:340,362; audits/2026-08-05-llm-context/SCHEMATIC.md:1554,1618).

Order of battle is static YAML: uk_forces with named units (HMS_Prince_of_Wales at Portsmouth with turns_to_full_readiness:3, 2 Type-45s, 2 Astutes, 2 SSBNs, 6 RAF squadrons at named bases), stockpiles with exact missile counts (96 Sea Viper, 30 Tomahawk...), red_forces (15 submarines, location: North_Atlantic_rendezvous, heading: southwest_toward_UK) — data/scenarios/war_game_2025/initial_conditions.yaml:83-294; served flattened (id/branch/type/location/status/readiness) by GET /game/{id}/resources (engine/game_manager.py:1018-1129, api/server.py:559-566).

State actors: 5 countries (USA, FRA, DEU, POL, RUS) with public + hidden state (true_motivations, hidden_agendas, redlines, threat_perception, capabilities 0-100) in data/state_actors.yaml, modeled by models/state_actors.py:6-117; each adjudication runs up to 3 relevant actors as LLM roleplays with their hidden state in-prompt (engine/actor_simulation.py:27-100,347).

Mystery Mode adds a secret NarrativeConfig (protagonist/antagonist/patsy + per-country FactionStance with secret_motive) from narratives.yaml that reaches ONLY actor-simulation and diplomacy prompts, never player-facing calls (models/narrative.py:44-150).

Event bus: every API session owns an asyncio.Queue; each event is stamped with layer, turn, t_plus_s (wall seconds since session start) and event_seq before SSE delivery (api/server.py:78-111); GET /stream/{session_id} serves it with server-side REFEREE filtering for non-facilitator sessions (api/server.py:823-869).

Six data layers tag all events: SITREP, INTEL, DIPLOMATIC, DOMESTIC, CABINET, REFEREE; inject 'channel' values map onto layers via CHANNEL_LAYER_MAP (models/layers.py:16-68). Layer tagging happens at the bus, never inside the engine.

EXCON seam: POST /game/{session_id}/inject fires a facilitator-authored inject (headline/content/channel/effects/target free-text) into a live session mid-turn via GameManager.deliver_inject — same primitives as scripted injects (transcript lines, metric effects, recent_injects, hidden-metrics sync) but deliberately NOT recorded in the event ledger; 403 unless the session was created with facilitator=true (api/control.py:127-208, engine/game_manager.py:260-315).

Headless demo driver: api/demo.py runs a daemon thread driving a full campaign (briefing -> answer mandatory call -> question -> interpret+commit) at a configurable pace_s, taking session.lock around every engine mutation and pushing through the same tagged bus (api/demo.py:69-167) — the existing template for any autonomous between-turn process.

Fictional clock: turns are ~2-3 fictional hours (turn 1 = Sun 5 Oct 2025 17:00, turn 2 = 19:00, turn 3 = 21:00, turn 4 = 00:00, turn 5 = 03:00 — episode file headers); game_time is a display string set once at init and never mechanically advanced (engine/game_manager.py:148-152, models/narrative_state.py:144).

Determinism is a design invariant: seeded Random(seed) per session, batch LLM calls pre-draw child seeds, RNG state is serialized in saves and restored after construction (engine/game_manager.py:62, 860, 936-940; engine/sim_loop.py:885-889 determinism gate).

12 LLM call families exist (LLMContext enum: advisor_qa, decision_interpretation, advisor_pushback, critical_omissions, inject_generation, diplomacy_conversation, diplomacy_outcome, character_response, quality_assessment, actor_simulation, situation_summary, narrator) with per-context runtime rerouting via POST /routing/{context} and hot-editable prompt templates via PUT /prompts/{family} (llm/model_config.py:11-24, api/control.py:22-263).

The DTDL worktree adds GET /dtdl and GET /dtdl/{dtmi} endpoints and 13 validated interfaces under dtmi:falseflag:* (Exercise, Inject, Timeline, Phase, Scenario, Scene, Participant, Role, LearningObjective, WorldReference, emergent:Session, emergent:AdjudicatedDecision, emergent:EventLedgerEntry); Session carries 9 telemetry streams (3 metrics, 2 casualties, inject_triggered, participant_action, phase_changed, advisor_trust) (dtdl-merged/api/server.py:1137-1250, interop/models/).

The dtmi:falseflag:WorldReference;1 interface has only string-typed 'location' and 'geographicScope' properties — no numeric coordinate schema exists in the DTDL layer either (interop/models/world_reference.json).
CORS is restricted to http://localhost:3000 and :3001 (api/server.py:39-45); sessions live in an in-memory dict with no persistence of the event stream (api/server.py:114).

A mandatory scripted diplomatic call blocks briefings and decisions with HTTP 409 until answered via /game/action/diplomacy/reply (api/server.py:1010-1024); the turn-6 US call is the campaign set-piece (turn_006.yaml).
geospatial: NO machine-readable coordinates exist anywhere in engine state, scenario data, injects, saves, or LLM prompts — no latitude/longitude, no GeoJSON, no map library, no grid/hex system (verified by repo-wide grep and confirmed by the repo's own audit: audits/2026-08-05-llm-context/data/agent-reports/synthesis.md:340,362).

Geography is REAL-WORLD but name-only: initial_conditions.yaml:304-322 lists 8 UK named locations (London, Faslane, RAF_Marham, East_Anglia_RAF_bases, Orkney_Islands, Portsmouth, Plymouth, UK_waters), 3 operational areas (North_Atlantic, GIUK_gap, International_waters), 1 Russian location (Severomorsk) — all real places, all plain strings, explicitly '(Not Hex Grid)'.

Unit positions are name-valued strings on static ORBAT entries: uk_forces[].location = Portsmouth/UK_waters/Faslane/RAF_Lossiemouth/RAF_Coningsby/RAF_Marham/RNAS_Yeovilton/available/classified; red_forces location = North_Atlantic_rendezvous with heading = southwest_toward_UK (initial_conditions.yaml:121-294). These never change during play — no movement model exists.

The only literal coordinates in the codebase are 3 hardcoded DMS strings for intro scene cards, explicitly 'presentation-layer flavour': Severomorsk 69°04'N 033°25'E, Northwood 51°38'N 000°28'W, COBRA/Whitehall 51°30'N 000°07'W (engine/opening.py:28-35).

Rich implicit geography lives in inject PROSE only: 'Kilo-class submarine surfaced 12 nautical miles off the Orkney Islands', MV Hamnavoe ferry Scrabster-Stromness, Scapa Flow, North Sea oil installations (turn_002.yaml), Drax power station (turn_003), RAF Fylingdales ballistic warning (turn_005), Heathrow diplomatic exodus — extractable only by NLP/LLM, not by parsing.

Scenario timeline is real-calendar fictional: October 2025, real UK bases and real force structures, fictional Russian operation ('Operation Tuman') — so REAL live GEOINT feeds would contradict the fiction; simulated feeds are the coherent choice.

WorldState.spatial_state (models/world.py:40) is a dormant location-name -> unit-ID dict that is serialized, saved and restored but never populated — an empty, engine-blessed slot for exactly the georeferenced unit-tracking a globe needs.

The stochastic scenario library carries location hints as string lists (e.g. submarine_surfacing locations: ['Orkney Islands', 'Scottish coast', 'English Channel'] — scenario_library.yaml), but the generated-inject YAML schema drops them: generated injects have no location field.

DTDL layer (worktree): WorldReference;1 'location'/'geographicScope' are string properties; Inject;1 has 'targets' but no geo schema — the twin model would need a new Geo interface or property additions for coordinates.
integration_hooks: SSE event bus (primary hook): GameSession.push_event / push_event_threadsafe with Layer tagging (api/server.py:78-111). An ambient GEOINT simulator can continuously push new event types (e.g. 'geo_track', 'sensor') onto a session's stream between turns WITHOUT touching engine state; every event already carries turn, t_plus_s wall-clock and event_seq, giving a Cesium clock a ready time axis. Adding a new Layer enum value (e.g. GEOINT) in models/layers.py:16-25 plus a CHANNEL_LAYER_MAP entry is a ~5-line change; _stream_filter (api/server.py:823-833) only drops REFEREE, so a new layer flows to players automatically.

Daemon-thread driver pattern (api/demo.py:69-167): the sanctioned template for a continuous between-turn process — a background thread bound to a session via llm_relay.bind, pacing with sleeps OUTSIDE session.lock and mutating the engine only under it. An 'ambient world ticker' (simulated flights/vessels/satellites drifting along tracks, occasional sensor events) is structurally identical to DemoRun.

GameManager.deliver_inject + POST /game/{session_id}/inject (engine/game_manager.py:260-315, api/control.py:140-208): the EXCON seam for ambient events that SHOULD touch game state (metric effects, advisor awareness via recent_injects) mid-turn, using the same primitives as scripted injects and correctly syncing hidden_metrics. Facilitator-flag gate (403) would need either a facilitator session per game or a new whitelisted ambient channel for player sessions.

WorldState.spatial_state (models/world.py:40): dead but fully serialized dict[location -> unit IDs]. A globe layer can claim it as the single source of truth for georeferenced unit positions (written by the ambient simulator, read by the globe renderer, round-trips through saves for free) with zero engine conflicts because nothing else reads it.

Static ORBAT + gazetteer: GET /game/{id}/resources already serves every UK unit with its named location and status (api/server.py:559-566, engine/game_manager.py:1018-1129); a small name->lat/lon gazetteer file for the ~15 named places in initial_conditions.yaml:304-322 plus base locations is sufficient to seed a 3D globe with the full starting picture (carrier at Portsmouth, squadrons at their real RAF bases, red fleet southwest of Iceland heading for the GIUK gap).

Turn-boundary window: between resolve_decision returning (phase='briefing', engine quiescent) and the client's next POST /game/{id}/briefing is entirely client-controlled dead time (api/server.py:872-916) — the natural slot for an XR 'between-inject' coordination phase of arbitrary real-time length; the engine cannot race it.

Inject channel/effects as visualization triggers: briefing_events and adjudication_events (api/server.py:141-228) already emit typed, layer-tagged events per inject/decision (channel, title, metric deltas on REFEREE, diplomatic cables per country, state_update with metrics) — a scene director can key camera moves and sensor-mode overlays (CRT/NVG/FLIR) off channel (flash_alert -> alarm mode) and layer with no engine change.

Metric telemetry for globe ambience: state_update events carry full metrics each turn (api/server.py:214-218); escalation_risk can drive globe-wide visual state (traffic density, military-flight ratio, sensor noise) exactly the way gods-eye-view layers toggle.

DTDL twin (worktree PRs #65/#66): /dtdl/{dtmi} endpoints and the emergent:Session interface's 9 telemetry streams (dtdl-merged/api/server.py:1137-1250) give a standards-shaped read model; a globe layer could be modeled as new dtmi:falseflag:geo:* interfaces and fed from the same bus, and the dashboard's DTDL live-count pattern (dashboard.html dtdlCounts wired to SSE events) shows the wiring precedent.

LLM extraction hook: inject prose is the richest location source; a new LLMContext (llm/model_config.py:11-24) e.g. GEO_EXTRACTION could post-process each inject into structured geo events (place, type, entity) using the existing router/reroute/prompt-template machinery — the control surface (api/control.py) would make its prompt hot-editable like every other family.

Scenario-authoring hook: episode YAML dicts pass through load_inject_for_turn unvalidated (engine/events.py:43-81 returns the raw dict), so adding an OPTIONAL 'geo:' block (entities, tracks, camera hints) to turn_NNN.yaml files is backward-compatible — the engine ignores unknown keys and the API can forward them in briefing_events.

Frontend seams: Next.js panel architecture (frontend/components/panels/*.tsx) for a globe panel in the player UI, and the self-contained no-build api/dashboard.html for a facilitator globe; CORS list (api/server.py:39-45) is the only server change a separate XR/WebXR origin needs.
risks: Ground-truth is prose, not structured state: the LLM narrative (situation_summary, inject descriptions) is the authoritative account of where things are ('12 nm off Orkney', 'submarines returning north' in endings). A globe that invents or extrapolates positions can visibly contradict the fiction; conversely nothing constrains the LLM to respect globe positions. Any geo layer needs either authored geo blocks per inject or an extraction step, plus acceptance that positions are decorative, not adjudicative.

Determinism invariant: sessions run on a seeded Random whose state is serialized in saves (engine/game_manager.py:860, 936-940) and there is an explicit determinism assertion (engine/sim_loop.py:885-889). An ambient layer MUST use its own RNG and never draw from the session RNG or reorder engine LLM calls, or saves/replays break.

Thread-safety is manual: GameManager has no internal locking; all mutation must hold GameSession.lock (api/server.py:64-69), and pacing/streaming must stay outside it (api/demo.py:73-76). A continuous ticker that mutates state without the lock can interleave read-then-write metric updates.

Hidden-metrics sync trap: any state change applied only to world.metrics is silently reverted when adjudication copies hidden_metrics back (engine/game_manager.py:296-307 documents this). Ambient effects must go through deliver_inject or replicate its sync, never poke world.metrics directly.

Ledger/continuity coupling: deliver_inject deliberately skips the event ledger because adjudication closes the most-recently-staged entry (engine/game_manager.py:273-280); a high-volume ambient event stream that DID enter the ledger or recent_injects would distort the do-not-restage machinery and the inject generator's continuity rules (llm/prompts.py rules 7-8). Ambient events should be stream-only by default.

Facilitator gate: the only mutating mid-turn inject path 403s non-facilitator sessions (api/control.py:156-161) and the flag is fixed at create time — piping ambient state changes into player sessions needs a deliberate new seam, which is also a security decision (the current design exists so a player session ID cannot rewrite its world).

Time-model mismatch: fictional time runs ~2-3 hours per turn and only as display strings (game_time never advances mechanically), while SSE t_plus_s is real wall-clock. A continuous globe needs an invented fictional clock interpolating between turn timestamps, and must freeze/slew it coherently across the discussion/decision phases whose fictional duration is undefined.

Real-world-content collision: the scenario uses real bases, real force structures and a real calendar (Oct 2025) with a fictional war; the gods-eye-view repo's LIVE feeds (real ADS-B/AIS/TLE) would show a peaceful 2026 reality under a fictional Russian fleet — simulated feeds are required (as planned), and mixing modes should be impossible by construction to avoid misinformation optics in a competition demo.

Session volatility: sessions and their event queues are in-memory only (api/server.py:114); an SSE reconnect replays nothing, so a globe client needs its own event journal or a new replay endpoint for late-joining XR viewers.

Merge-timing risk: the feasibility work targets the dtdl-merged worktree (PRs #65/#66) whose api/server.py diverges from main (adds /dtdl routes at :1137-1250); building the globe layer against main's server risks conflicts in the same file both efforts touch.

Scale/pacing of the LLM loop: a full turn involves ~10+ LLM calls (interpretation, pushback, omissions, quality, up-to-3 actors, reactions, summary) and can take minutes on real providers — the ambient layer must be engaging for multi-minute gaps and degrade gracefully when WARGAME_LLM=mock (instant turns) compresses them to seconds.
CORS/hosting: allow_origins is hardcoded to localhost:3000/3001 (api/server.py:39-45); an XR headset client or hosted Cesium page on another origin fails silently until this is widened.

readers.summary: The FALSE FLAG API layer (/home/user/false-flag/api/) is a FastAPI wrapper around the in-process GameManager engine: each HTTP session owns a GameSession holding one GameManager, a threading.Lock, and a single asyncio.Queue that serves as the event bus. Every event is stamped at the bus (never in the engine) with one of six data layers (SITREP/INTEL/DIPLOMATIC/DOMESTIC/CABINET/REFEREE), turn number, wall-clock T+ seconds, and a per-session sequence number, then streamed to clients over one SSE endpoint (GET /stream/{session_id}) with REFEREE events server-filtered out of non-facilitator streams. Facilitator seams are POST /game/{id}/inject (deliver_inject with metric effects, facilitator sessions only), the /routing reroute matrix, /prompts hot-edit, and a headless /demo/start driver that animates a full campaign unattended. An external CesiumJS or Unity client could subscribe to the SSE stream today with a session id and no auth, but would find: no geographic fields anywhere in events (locations are free-text UK/NATO place names in YAML/prose), a single-consumer queue that makes a second concurrent stream client steal events from the first, no event replay, no WebSocket/bidirectional channel, no simulated clock or interpolation hints, and CORS locked to localhost:3000/3001 for browser clients.
facts: EVENT BUS: GameSession (api/server.py:48-111) holds one asyncio.Queue per session; _make_item (api/server.py:78-97) stamps every event with layer (default SITREP), turn, t_plus_s (wall-clock seconds since session start, 3dp), and event_seq (monotonic per session), JSON-serializes the payload, and carries a server-side-only _layer key that the stream filter pops before yield.

EVENT TYPES published on the bus (complete set): 'transcript' (data.type one of scene/inject/system/narrator/advisor/error), 'system', 'state_update' ({phase, turn, metrics{escalation_risk,domestic_stability,alliance_cohesion,casualties_civ,casualties_mil}}), 'diplomacy' ({type:'call_started'|'call_turn', country/title/transcript or lines/active/outcome}), 'intel' ({type:'assessment_pulled', actor, code, confidence}), 'ending', plus REFEREE-only: 'adjudication' (raw effects/pushback/critical_concerns/error), 'parse_health', 'llm_call' (family/tier/provider/model/latency_ms/fallback/prompt_chars/reply_chars — no prompt bodies), 'inject_fired' (facilitator inject record with raw effects).

LAYER TAGS: models/layers.py defines Layer enum {sitrep,intel,diplomatic,domestic,cabinet,referee}; CHANNEL_LAYER_MAP (models/layers.py:37-53) maps inject 'channel' values (briefing/emergency/flash_alert/military/breaking→SITREP, intelligence/intel→INTEL, diplomatic→DIPLOMATIC, media→DOMESTIC); layer_for_channel canonicalises case/hyphens, unknown→SITREP. The referenced DATA_LAYERS.md doc does not exist as a file in the repo — it lives only in code comments.

PUBLISH MECHANICS: async endpoints call session.push_event(); worker threads (demo driver, LLM relay) call push_event_threadsafe() which uses loop.call_soon_threadsafe (api/server.py:104-111). Two pure mapper functions are the single source of event shapes: briefing_events (api/server.py:141-157) and adjudication_events (api/server.py:160-228). The engine itself never publishes — the API layer maps GameManager return values onto events; the terminal CLI (cli/main.py) and the Pyodide browser build (docs/py/bridge.py) drive the engine in-process and bypass the API entirely.

STREAMING: exactly one streaming endpoint — GET /stream/{session_id} (api/server.py:836-869), SSE via sse_starlette EventSourceResponse; each item is a named SSE event (event: <type>, data: <json>); 1.0s queue timeout emits ': keep-alive' comments; EventSource auto-reconnect relied on client-side. NO WebSocket anywhere in the codebase. NO auth of any kind — the UUID4 session_id is the only capability; CORS allowlist is hardcoded to http://localhost:3000 and http://localhost:3001 (api/server.py:39-45).

STREAM FILTERING: _stream_filter (api/server.py:823-833) drops REFEREE items for sessions not created with facilitator=true; the flag is fixed at POST /game/new (body field or query param, api/server.py:445-466) with deliberately no way to escalate a live session; the layer value also travels inside the JSON payload so clients filter/colour without parsing conventions.

CRITICAL QUEUE SEMANTICS: the event bus is a single asyncio.Queue consumed destructively by the stream generator — two simultaneous SSE clients on one session each steal a share of events (no fan-out); events also queue unboundedly when no client is attached (demo driver keeps pushing).

SESSION/CATCH-UP: sessions dict is in-memory only (api/server.py:114); GET /game/{session_id} (api/server.py:525-543) returns full transcript + active_call for resumption; GET /game/{id}/state returns the raw WorldState dict including spatial_state; polling endpoints: /game/{id}/resources (ForceUnit has location: Optional[str] — named places like Faslane, RAF_Marham), /diplomacy/contacts, /state/vibes, /state/advisors, /state/flags, /intel, /intel/{actor}.

TURN LOOP over HTTP: POST /game/new (turn 1 briefing incl. opening scenes) → POST /game/{id}/briefing (later turns) → POST /game/{id}/briefing/ack (phase→discussion) → POST /game/discussion (advisor Q&A; advisor:'all' fans out) → POST /game/decision/interpret → POST /game/decision/commit (or legacy one-shot POST /game/decision) → adjudication events streamed. _require_no_mandatory_call (api/server.py:1010-1024) 409s decisions while a scripted mandatory diplomatic call is live; the call is driven via POST /game/action/call and /game/action/diplomacy/reply, both mirrored onto the DIPLOMATIC layer.

FACILITATOR CONTROL SURFACE (api/control.py): POST /game/{session_id}/inject (403 unless session.facilitator) builds an inject {id:'manual_<ts>', title, channel, description, effects:[{metric,delta}]} and calls GameManager.deliver_inject under session.lock, then pushes a 'transcript' event (manual:true) on the channel's layer plus an 'inject_fired' REFEREE record; GET/POST/DELETE /routing/{context} = runtime per-LLM-context model override matrix (12 contexts); GET/PUT/DELETE /prompts/{family} = hot-edit prompt templates with placeholder validation.

GameManager.deliver_inject (engine/game_manager.py:260-315) reuses the briefing primitives (display_inject + apply_inject_effects), appends to world.recent_injects (last 5), syncs hidden metrics, and is deliberately NOT recorded in the played-event ledger (would corrupt the one-entry-per-turn adjudication disposition); returns {title, channel, lines}.

DEMO DRIVER (api/demo.py): POST /demo/start creates a facilitator session and a daemon thread that runs briefing → mandatory-call answer → cabinet question → interpret+commit decision for N turns (1-30) at pace_s (0-30s), pushing through the same tagged bus; returns {session_id, stream:'/stream/{id}'}; POST /demo/{id}/stop and GET /demo/{id}/status; WARGAME_LLM=mock makes it free/deterministic — this is a ready-made 'attract mode' feed for an XR/globe demo.

LLM RELAY (api/llm_relay.py): every router-dispatched model call is forwarded from llm/call_log.py to the bound session as a REFEREE 'llm_call' event via a contextvar binding (bind(session_id) in _session_or_404 and the demo thread); forwarded fields: seq, ts, turn, family, tier, provider, model, finish_reason, latency_ms, fallback, batch_index, batch_size, plus prompt_chars/reply_chars.

DASHBOARD (api/dashboard.html, served at GET /dashboard, self-contained, no build step): header session controls (new facilitator session / demo start / attach by id) + clickable six-layer legend; panels = event ledger (newest-first, max 400 rows, per-layer show/hide, layer chip + channel + turn + T+ + seq per row), SVG metric traces fed by 'state_update', llm_call feed (max 80), routing matrix table, inject console form, prompt editor. connectStream() (dashboard.html:317-330) registers EventSource listeners for the 10 event names and dispatches into addLedgerRow/recordMetrics/addCallCard.

DATAFLOW PAGE (api/dataflow.html, GET /dataflow): a hand-laid SVG schema of ~30 code-anchored nodes and edges (drag-to-tidy, layout in localStorage under 'ff-dataflow-layout-v1'); attaches to the same /stream/{id}, pulses nodes on 'llm_call' by family (CTX_NODE map) and pulses the bus node on all other event types; per-node side panel exposes live call counts, reroute controls (POST /routing/{ctx}) and prompt hot-edit; includes a 17-step guided walkthrough filtered by game mode.

GEO ABSENCE: no latitude/longitude/geojson fields exist in any model, event, or endpoint. readers.summary: The interop/ worktree holds a DTDL v3 model set of 13 interfaces in the dtmi:falseflag namespace (7 model files), structurally validated by a stdlib validator and parsed clean by Microsoft's official DTDLParser (278 entities, zero errors). The domain splits into a scenario-side graph (Exercise -> Timeline -> Phase -> Scenario -> Scene, plus Role/Participant/Inject/WorldReference/LearningObjective) and an emergent-assessment run-side graph (Session with 9 turn-indexed telemetry streams, AdjudicatedDecision, EventLedgerEntry). export_run.py captures a deterministic mock campaign through the real GameManager and exports two Azure-DT-style instance documents ($metadata.$model bindings); api/server.py serves the models and real sample instances at GET /dtdl and /dtdl/{dtmi}, while live play flows over a separate layer-tagged SSE stream (/stream/{session_id}) that a globe/XR client would actually subscribe to. Geospatially the twin is entirely symbolic: real UK/Russia place names as free strings (WorldReference.location/geographicScope, the scenario YAML locations block, red-force heading strings) with zero coordinates and no DTDL geospatial schemas or semantic types anywhere, so a 3D-globe layer needs a gazetteer plus a new GeoAsset-style interface with plain double lat/lon/alt telemetry (the ADT-safe encoding) and updates to the local validator and the hard-coded 9-stream/13-interface assertions. DTDL compliance is a genuine strength for the AI Challenge story (official-parser-clean, ADT-uploadable, versioned additive extension), but ADT is optional - the globe can consume /dtdl + SSE directly - and the turn-based batch-export cadence means all real-time motion between injects must be simulated presentation-layer interpolation, not recorded twin data.

gods-eye-view (MIT, 10.5k stars, vanilla JS + CesiumJS 1.124 + Vite 6, single-author v0.1.0) is a browser 3D-globe GEOINT viewer whose 13 live layers are plain JS module objects registered with a ~2,250-line DataLayerManager that owns all polling; every layer fetches through relative /api/* routes brokered by ~3,500 lines of Vite middleware, giving two clean seams for FALSE FLAG: register new simulated layer modules client-side, or serve scripted OpenSky/AIS/USGS-shaped JSON at the existing /api/* routes with zero client changes. A precedent already exists in-repo: the traffic layer runs a full deterministic simulation whenever no TomTom key is present and labels it "SIMULATED — add TomTom key for live", and honest labeling of modeled data is a stated design principle, though there is no general replay/offline mode. The SceneDirector is a deterministic, JSON-serializable cutscene engine (scenes→shots with camera lat/lon/alt/heading/pitch/roll, per-shot duration/hold, visual style, and layer toggles; import/export, live captureShot, 5 built-in recipes) that is directly reusable for inject cinematics but requires the styleManager living inside the 10,293-line ui.js monolith; the six sensor styles (thermal/FLIR, retro/CRT, surveillance/NVG, noir, anime, snow) are self-contained Cesium PostProcessStage GLSL modules portable to any Cesium viewer. Costs are avoidable: only GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY is code-required (a missing-var throw halts init, but a caught tileset failure falls back to a free OSM/Cesium-globe mode, so a dummy key or 3-line patch yields a $0 deployment), OpenAI voice is cleanly severable (~5.3k lines), and simulating feeds moots every data key and most data-license risk — except TeleGeography submarine cables (CC BY-NC-SA, must delete for commercial use) and required on-globe attribution credits. Biggest gaps for the FALSE FLAG use case: no VR/WebXR support at all, real-Earth-only WGS84 geography while FALSE FLAG stores locations as free-text names with zero numeric coordinates, and extraction of a globe+layers core is realistically 15–25k LOC of tightly hand-tuned code.
facts: Q1 LAYER CONTRACT — Layers are plain JS objects, no base class (src/data/manager.js, ~2,250 lines). Required: id (stable string), name, icon, source, init(viewer,{signal}), enable(viewer,{signal}), disable(viewer), update(viewer,{signal}). Optional: destroy, getStats()->{count,lastUpdate,status,error,loading}, setParams/getParams, getRowControls()->{chips,legend}, setLifecyclePresentation, refreshInterval (preferred) or updateInterval in ms (0 = self-managed, e.g. traffic), statsRefreshInterval (default 1000ms), showInTogglePanel (default true).

Q1 SCHEDULING — Manager-owned polling: per-layer `entry.intervalId = setInterval(() => { void this._runPeriodicUpdate(layerId, entry); }, refreshInterval)`; layers do not self-schedule. Toggles serialized per-layer via _enqueueToggle with lifecycle states 'disabled'|'enabled'|'enabling'|'disabling', AbortController supersession, and intent epochs. Registration: `dataManager.register(layerObj)` per layer in src/main.js (~460 lines), then `dataManager.finalizeRegistrations(LAYER_STATE_REGISTRY)` from src/data/layerState.js; enabled-state persisted under key gev:layer-state:v2 (origins user/voice/tool).

Q1 ENTITY SCHEMA — No manager-level entity schema; each layer owns its rendering. flights.js (~4,000 lines) keeps Map<icao24,{callsign,altitude,velocity,true_track,onGround,klass,typeCode,registration,airline,route,rawLat,rawLon,renderAltitudeM,lastContactEpochMs,turnRateDps,...}> plus per-aircraft position history (JulianDate+Cartesian3, cap 5) in one GPU-batched BillboardCollection (5000+ sprites) with optional glTF models (cap 150/350). earthquakes.js (~365 lines) is the minimal example: {id:'earthquakes', name:'Earthquakes (24h)', icon, source:'USGS', updateInterval:60000, init/enable/disable/update/destroy/getStats} rendering CLAMP_TO_GROUND ellipses in a CustomDataSource from https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/feed/v1.0/summary/all_day.geojson.

Q1 DEAD-RECKONING — Implemented inside flights.js, not the manager: render clock runs RENDER_DELAY_SEC=30s behind wall time so positions interpolate between two known fixes (lerp on bracketing history pair); when no bracket exists, ENU constant-turn-rate arc extrapolation (arcOffsetEnu(speed,heading,turnRateDps,dt) + eastNorthUpToFixedFrame); new fixes absorbed via _drCorrection decayed over DR_CORRECTION_MS=900ms; heading blends segment chord with reported track. A simulated feed emitting fixes every 15–30s inherits smooth motion for free.

Q2 FEED REPLACEMENT — Every live layer fetches RELATIVE proxy paths served by Vite middleware in vite.config.js (~3,500 lines): /api/opensky?lat&lon (OpenSky states shape), /api/adsb.lol, /api/adsbdb/type|route, /api/aisstream (server holds websocket, browser polls a 50,000-vessel cache), /api/celestrak (TLEs), /api/firms, /api/tomtom (+/status -> {hasKey,...}), /api/overpass, /api/radio, /api/gbfs, /api/launches, /api/cctv, /api/terrain/heights, /api/nominatim, /api/weather. Replacing these handlers with a FALSE FLAG scenario feed server that emits the same JSON shapes requires zero client-side changes.

Q2 EXISTING SIMULATION PRECEDENT — traffic.js (~2,400 lines) already ships a full keyless simulation: deterministic per-road-class speeds/densities over real OSM Overpass geometry, dots at randomized positions/speeds (+/-30%), altitude-adaptive spacing; mode decided by one call to /api/tomtom/status (`_liveMode = Boolean(status?.hasKey)`); UI label 'SIMULATED — add TomTom key for live' vs 'LIVE · TomTom flow'. README codifies honest labeling ('a labeled simulation', 'RECONSTRUCTED ESTIMATE'). However there is NO general replay/record mode and docs/CURRENT-STATE.md documents no offline mode; src/data/fixtures and scripts/opensky-import-client.sh are test/import tooling, not runtime replay.

Q3 SCENE DIRECTOR — src/scenes/director.js (~1,200 lines): startScene(sceneId,{single}), stopScene(reason), loadShot, runNextScene, captureShot (snapshots live camera+visual+layer state into a shot), updateSelectedShot, exportProject/importProjectFile (JSON, PROJECT_VERSION=3, migration handled), downloadLastRunMetadata. Scene shape: {id,title,shots:[{id,title,durationSec,holdSec,camera:{lat,lon,alt,heading,pitch,roll},visual:{style,bloom,sharpen,hud,detection,styleParams},layers:{layerId:{enabled,params?}}}]}; cubic ease-in-out flyTo then hold; 3-layer cancellation (token+AbortSignal+generation counter); camera-ownership claim prevents jitter. src/scenes/recipes.js (~165 lines) exports SCENE_RECIPES: flights-radar, orbital-watch, thermal-threats, city-overload, omniscience-pullback. Deterministic and fully scriptable from JSON — directly usable for inject cinematics — but constructor requires (viewer, styleManager, dataManager); cannot run on a bare Cesium viewer.

Q3 SENSOR MODES — src/styles/{thermal,noir,retro,surveillance,anime,snow}.js are self-contained Cesium PostProcessStage definitions ({name, uniforms, fragmentShader} GLSL strings); thermal.js (~450 lines) has sensitivity/bloom/white-hot-black-hot mode/pixelation/FLIR-vs-Ironbow palette uniforms and needs only the standard colorTexture binding — portable to ANY Cesium viewer including a FALSE FLAG-native one. ui.js confirms PostProcessStage application with intensity crossfade. docs/CURRENT-STATE.md: visual presets Normal/CRT/NVG/FLIR/Anime/Noir/Snow; detection overlays with CRT/NVG/FLIR presets; a first-person cockpit view (cockpitTracking.js 92 lines coordinating layer.trackById/stopTracking + cockpitView.enter/exit, plus ~10 cockpit* modules) with its own CRT/NVG/FLIR vision cycle.

Q4 KEYS/COSTS — .env.example: required GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY (client-exposed); optional CESIUM_ION_TOKEN, OPENAI_API_KEY(+7 voice tuning vars), OPENSKY_CLIENT_ID/SECRET, FIRMS_MAP_KEY, AISSTREAM_API_KEY, TOMTOM_API_KEY. main.js THROWS 'GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY not found' when the env var is UNSET (halting init) — but tileset creation failure is caught: 'Google 3D Tiles unavailable, falling back to Cesium globe' and boot continues with MapStackController initialStack = tileset ? 'photoreal' : 'osm'. mapStackController.js (~370 lines) supports google-photoreal / bing-aerial / bing-labels (ion token) / OSM; keyless terrain = Re:Earth (CC BY 4.0) with EllipsoidTerrainProvider fallback. So: dummy key or trivial patch -> $0 run on OSM globe. Google 3D tiles ~$6/1,000 root tileset requests after 1,000 free/month; OpenAI voice metered (session-capped $5) and optional; with FALSE FLAG-simulated feeds ALL data keys become unnecessary.

designs.thesis: The turn-quantized engine's dead time is the product, not the problem: between resolve_decision (engine/game_manager.py:590-592) and the next POST /game/{id}/briefing nothing runs, which means an ambient, continuously-simulated photorealistic globe can own that window completely without ever racing the engine. Build a two-clock, two-renderer architecture: the Python engine stays the turn-quantized narrative authority emitting geo KEYFRAMES at inject/adjudication boundaries; a vendored gods-eye-view core (DataLayerManager + SceneDirector + GLSL sensor stages, all feeds replaced by FALSE FLAG-simulated ones) renders the shared operational picture on desktop CesiumJS; a three.js + 3DTilesRendererJS WebXR war-room table renders the same event bus in-headset (CesiumJS's own VR mode is honestly rejected below). Escalation_risk drives the sensor-mode shader as a DEFCON-style game state (normal -> CRT -> NVG -> FLIR), inject delivery drives scene-director cinematic fly-ins, and the whole thing is DTDL-modeled as dtmi:falseflag:geo:* twins with explicit simulated-provenance — turning FALSE FLAG from a text game with a dashboard into an LLM-driven digital-twin crisis theatre, which is exactly the 'think big' story an AI Challenge jury can see from the back of the room.
designs.architecture:
FIVE PLANES, ONE BUS.

PLANE 1 — NARRATIVE AUTHORITY (Python engine, untouched golden code). engine/, models/, data/ remain protected per the owner's Golden Code rules (UX/UI/WebApp/00_MASTER_DEV_PLAN.md:113-125). The engine stays strictly turn-quantized: briefing -> discussion -> decision -> adjudication (models/world.py:15, engine/game_manager.py:182-614). The ONLY engine-adjacent write is populating the already-serialized, confirmed-dead WorldState.spatial_state dict (models/world.py:40 — verified never read/written, audits/2026-08-05-llm-context/data/agent-reports/synthesis.md:340) with location->unit-ID membership at each keyframe, behind a WARGAME_GEO=1 feature flag. Everything else lives in a new geo/ package OUTSIDE the engine.

PLANE 2 — GEO KEYFRAME + AMBIENT SIMULATION (new Python package geo/, runs in the FastAPI process). Three modules: (a) geo/gazetteer.py loads data/scenarios/war_game_2025/gazetteer.yaml — a NEW authored file mapping the ~20 named places (initial_conditions.yaml:305-323 locations block + base names on uk_forces entries + Severomorsk) to WGS84 lat/lon/alt, plus polygon 'operational areas' for North_Atlantic, GIUK_gap, UK_waters. (b) geo/keyframes.py builds a GeoKeyframe at every turn boundary: it merges (i) an OPTIONAL authored 'geo:' block in episode YAML (backward-compatible — engine/events.py:43-81 returns the raw dict, unknown keys ignored), (ii) the static ORBAT from GameManager.get_resources (engine/game_manager.py:1018-1129) seeded through the gazetteer, and (iii) for stochastic turns (>=7) an LLM geo-extraction pass over the inject prose using a NEW LLMContext GEO_EXTRACTION added to llm/model_config.py:11-24, hot-editable via the existing PUT /prompts/{family} machinery (api/control.py). Keyframes carry a FICTIONAL timestamp taken from the episode-header clock (turn 1 = Sun 5 Oct 2025 17:00, ~2-3h per turn). (c) geo/ambient.py is a WorldSim daemon thread cloned from the sanctioned api/demo.py pattern (bind, sleep OUTSIDE session.lock, push via push_event_threadsafe api/server.py:104-111): it owns its OWN random.Random (never the session RNG — determinism invariant, engine/game_manager.py:62,936-940) and continuously emits simulated tracks: the red Northern Fleet formation advancing along an authored North_Atlantic_rendezvous -> GIUK_gap -> UK_waters spline (initial_conditions.yaml:268-296 gives 15 vessels, heading southwest_toward_UK), RAF QRA orbits and P-8 racetracks from base positions, procedural civil ADS-B/AIS chaff whose density is a function of escalation_risk (airspace empties as the crisis deepens), a fixed authored TLE set for satellite passes, and scripted SIGINT/'CCTV' point events tied to inject channels. These are STREAM-ONLY events: they never enter the ledger, recent_injects, or metrics (avoiding the hidden-metrics revert trap at engine/game_manager.py:296-307 and the ledger disposition machinery at :273-280).

PLANE 3 — BUS UPGRADES (api/server.py + models/layers.py). designs.name: TWIN THEATRE — DTDL-as-Contract Geospatial Layer
designs.thesis: Make the Microsoft-DTDLParser-validated DTDL model the single contract for everything spatial: extend dtmi:falseflag with a small geo namespace (GeoLocation gazetteer twins, TheatreEntity assets with plain-double position telemetry, a per-session Theatre sidecar twin carrying geo telemetry streams), have a deterministic 'World Simulator' service instantiate those twins from the existing ORBAT YAML and emit twin telemetry over the existing layer-tagged SSE bus between turns, and build the globe (and later the VR client) as pure DTDL-twin renderers that discover models at GET /dtdl and route events by DTMI. The engine's golden code stays geo-ignorant; positions are explicitly modeled as simulated telemetry with provenance (simulated:true), honoring the owner's 'wire, never fabricate' ruling instead of violating it. The judging story is unmatched — 'the same twin graph runs locally over SSE and uploads to Azure Digital Twins unchanged' — and VR becomes a third renderer of the same contract rather than a Cesium fork. The honest cost: roughly +30-40% effort over a hardcoded globe (interface authoring, DTDL version discipline, validator/test/README churn, renderer indirection), which is worth paying only because the twin model IS the entry's differentiator.
designs.architecture:
FOUR TIERS, ONE CONTRACT. The contract is DTDL v3 interfaces in interop/models/ plus a twin-change wire protocol over the existing SSE bus; every tier above the engine speaks only that contract.

== TIER 1: DTDL MODEL EXTENSION (interop/models/geo.json, one new file) ==
The /dtdl endpoint globs interop/models/*.json and auto-serves/auto-counts anything dropped there (dtdl-merged/api/server.py:1153-1163), so new interfaces need zero registration. Add 4 interfaces in a dtmi:falseflag:geo namespace, all @context dtmi:dtdl:context;3, all plain primitives — deliberately NOT DTDL geospatial schemas or Latitude/Longitude semantic co-types, because (a) validate_dtdl.py's check_element rejects co-typed @type arrays and 'point' is not in PRIMITIVE_SCHEMAS (verified: interop/validate_dtdl.py:30,178), so plain doubles require ZERO validator changes, and (b) plain doubles are the ADT-safe encoding (ADT geospatial schemas are Telemetry-only and unqueryable). Interfaces:

== TURN/REAL-TIME RECONCILIATION ==
Two clocks, explicitly modeled. Engine time is turn-indexed (all DTDL telemetry stamps 'T+n'); the bus stamps wall-clock t_plus_s. world_sim maintains fic_time = episode_timestamp(turn) + ratio * wall_seconds_in_turn, clamped to the next episode timestamp (turn 1 = Sun 5 Oct 2025 17:00 etc. from episode headers); every position fix carries {turn, sim_time}. Between resolve_decision returning and the next POST /briefing the engine is provably quiescent (api/server.py:872-916), so the between-turn window is arbitrarily long and race-free — the world_sim fills it, and the globe HUD shows fic_time as the theatre clock.

verified.claim: CesiumJS can deliver a working in-headset VR/WebXR experience today (2026).
verified.evidence: CesiumJS has no WebXR support as of v1.144 (current, 2026). Scene.useWebVR (docs, 1.144) is a legacy side-by-side viewport split "used for cardboard and WebVR" — no WebXR session, no headset pose tracking, no lens distortion correction; the WebVR API it targets was removed from all major browsers ~2020, so on a Quest the page stays a flat 2D panel (only phone-in-Cardboard 'works', poorly). The WebXR feature request (CesiumGS/cesium#3422) has been open since Jan 13, 2016 (roadmap label, unimplemented). The only implementation attempt, PR #11372 'initial WebXR display support' (opened Jun 27, 2023), is still OPEN, self-described proof-of-concept with framebuffer/antialiasing and camera-matrix defects; Cesium staff said in Oct 2024 they "haven't been able to prioritize getting this merged", and the latest activity (Sep 22, 2025) is a user asking for it. Issue #11298 shows hand-rolled WebXR around viewer.scene.render() failing, closed unsolved. gods-eye-view itself (fetched README) is CesiumJS + Google Photorealistic 3D Tiles in vanilla JS with zero VR/WebXR mention. Alternatives verified: NASA-AMMOS/3DTilesRendererJS is actively maintained (~3,000 commits), has three.js/Babylon.js/R3F renderers, loads Google Photorealistic 3D Tiles and Cesium ion, and ships a working WebXR example (example/three/vr.html + vr.js); Babylon.js 9.0 (Mar 2026) added official 3D Tiles support (its docs recommend the 3DTilesRendererJS babylon renderer) plus a Geospatial Camera, and Babylon's WebXR is first-class; Cesium for Unity officially supports Quest 2/Quest Pro via OpenXR (cesium-unity-samples has Quest APK instructions); Cesium for Unreal has an official 'Build for Quest' standalone-APK tutorial requiring heavy compromises (max SSE 256, forward shading, unlit materials). Local repo /home/user/false-flag contains no Cesium/XR code — all claim facts are external.
conditions: Do NOT build the VR path on CesiumJS or wait for its WebXR PR (#11372) — it is an unmerged, deprioritized proof-of-concept after 3 years; treat CesiumJS as desktop/mobile-flat only.

Recommended path for a small team: three.js + NASA-AMMOS 3DTilesRendererJS with three.js's built-in WebXR (renderer.xr + VRButton), served to Quest Browser — a working VR example (example/three/vr.html) already exists; reuse gods-eye-view's data-layer fetch logic (flights/ships/satellites) but re-render entities in three.js; none of its Cesium rendering code carries over.
Photorealistic 3D Tiles on standalone Quest browser work but need aggressive screen-space-error tuning and layer throttling; expect reduced tile quality at street level and budget a performance pass.

If you need native performance headroom, hand tracking, or app-store distribution: Cesium for Unity on Quest via OpenXR is the supported native route (Cesium for Unreal also works but is heavier tooling for a small team); both demand rendering compromises on standalone Quest per Cesium's own tutorials.

Babylon.js is now a viable second web option (9.0+, Mar 2026: 3D Tiles via the 3DTilesRendererJS babylon renderer + Geospatial Camera + mature WebXR), but the three.js renderer of 3DTilesRendererJS is older and more battle-tested; only pick Babylon if the team already knows it.
Cesium's 'cardboard/VR mode' (Scene.useWebVR / vrButton) may only be pitched as a novelty phone-in-cardboard mode, never as headset support.
