ideas.mechanism: Episode YAML passes through engine/events.py:43-81 unvalidated (raw dict returned, unknown keys ignored), so each turn_NNN.yaml gains an optional backward-compatible 'geo:' block: entities, lat/lon anchor, and a camera-hint recipe. The briefing_events mapper (api/server.py:141-157) — the declared single source of event shape for both async endpoints and the demo thread — forwards it on the inject transcript event. The globe client converts it into a SceneDirector project (src/scenes/director.js, PROJECT_VERSION 3: shots with camera lat/lon/alt/heading/pitch/roll, durationSec/holdSec, visual style, per-layer toggles) and calls importProjectFile + startScene. Channel drives treatment via the existing CHANNEL_LAYER_MAP vocabulary (models/layers.py:37-53): flash_alert -> hard cut + alarm ring + thermal; intelligence -> slow NVG orbit; diplomatic -> capital-to-capital arc. For stochastic turns 7+ where injects are LLM-generated prose with no location field (llm/inject_generator.py:37-138), add a GEO_EXTRACTION LLMContext to llm/model_config.py:11-24 that post-processes each inject into {place, entity, type} using the existing routing/hot-editable-prompt machinery (api/control.py) — one extra cheap LLM call per turn.
ideas.payoff: The single biggest felt upgrade per line of authored content: the six scripted turns become directed set-pieces (the turn_002 Orkney surfacing, turn_003 Drax, turn_005 Fylingdales), and the authoring cost is a ~10-line YAML block per episode using a proven, importable cutscene format.

ideas.title: DEFCON shader coupling: escalation-driven sensor modes plus the fictional day-night clock
ideas.description: Tie the globe's entire visual register to the two axes the game already computes: escalation_risk selects the sensor mode (clean satellite view at low tension, CRT at guarded, NVG/FLIR as war approaches), and the fictional clock drives real sun position — the campaign runs Sun 5 Oct 17:00 through 03:00, so turns 4-5 play in literal darkness where NVG is the only honest view. Rising escalation is something the player sees before reading a single number.
ideas.mechanism: state_update events already carry full metrics every turn (api/server.py:214-218), mirrored by the DTDL Session;1 escalation_risk telemetry stream (interop/models/session.json) for a standards-shaped binding. Banded thresholds swap gods-eye-view's self-contained PostProcessStage GLSL modules (src/styles/thermal.js, retro.js, surveillance.js — plain {name, uniforms, fragmentShader} objects portable to any Cesium viewer, no ui.js needed). Shader tint uniforms read the active theme's CSS tokens: frontend theme-retro's 120-degree phosphor green (globals.css:32-154) IS an NVG palette and theme-defcon's cyan a CRT palette, so globe and DOM chrome shift together through the existing SettingsPanel switcher. This literally implements the roadmap line in docs/AESTHETIC_LANGUAGE.md — 'wire fog density to escalation risk' (density = escalation_risk/100). The fictional clock comes from episode-header times (turn 1 = 17:00 ... turn 5 = 03:00); set Cesium's simulation clock to the fictional date/time each briefing and slew it across the between-turn window, so the day-night terminator, city lights, and sun angle track the story instead of real 2026 wall-clock.
ideas.payoff: Highest feel-per-effort ratio in the set: zero backend changes (events already carry everything), and it converts abstract 0-100 gauges into visceral atmosphere — playtesters will describe escalation as 'the world going green-and-grainy' rather than 'the number went up'.

ideas.title: Fog-of-war globe: intelligence-confidence rendering with a REFEREE ground-truth god view
ideas.description: The player never sees the Russian fleet — they see what UK intelligence believes: aging ghost contacts, uncertainty ellipses that bloom with time-since-fix and tighten with assessment confidence, a probability cone sweeping toward the GIUK gap. The facilitator's globe, on the same session, renders crisp ground truth. The gap between the two views IS the game's hidden-information design, made spatial.
ideas.mechanism: The server-side layer fence already exists: _stream_filter (api/server.py:823-833) strips REFEREE from non-facilitator streams, and the facilitator flag is fixed at session creation (api/server.py:445-466). Publish red-force truth tracks as REFEREE-layer geo events (facilitator globe renders them directly) and player-facing estimates as INTEL-layer events carrying a confidence value — reusing the shape of the existing 'intel' event ({type:'assessment_pulled', actor, code, confidence}) and engine/intelligence.py's deterministic hidden-metric-to-prose reads as the confidence source. The ambient simulator (idea 1's thread) degrades the estimate: position error and ellipse radius grow between 'fixes', and a fix event snaps them tight — visually identical to real GEOINT track handling. Seed truth from initial_conditions.yaml:268-296 (7 SSBN + 8 SSN, location North_Atlantic_rendezvous, heading southwest_toward_UK). Mystery Mode's NarrativeConfig already never reaches player-facing LLM calls (models/narrative.py:44-150) — the same fence keeps the antagonist's assets REFEREE-only. Units whose ORBAT location is 'classified' (SSBN on patrol) are rendered as a patrol-box annotation, never a point.
ideas.payoff: Makes FALSE FLAG's core epistemic tension (you act on beliefs, not truth) visible and dramatic; doubles as the facilitator/EXCON killer demo — two screens, same session, different realities — which is a strong competition-judging moment.

ideas.title: Ride the patrol: cockpit ride-alongs on real ORBAT assets between turns
ideas.description: While adjudication grinds, the player can 'join' a simulated P-8 Poseidon out of RAF Lossiemouth sweeping the GIUK gap, or a QRA Typhoon pair from RAF Coningsby — first-person cockpit camera with the CRT/NVG/FLIR vision cycle, watching the same ambient tracks the watch floor shows from orbit. When the next inject involves something at sea (the Kilo off Orkney), the simulator can route the patrol for a flyby so the player glimpses it from the cockpit before the formal briefing names it.
ideas.mechanism: gods-eye-view ships this nearly whole: cockpitTracking.js (92 lines) coordinates layer.trackById/stopTracking with cockpitView.enter/exit plus ~10 cockpit* modules and a per-mode CRT/NVG/FLIR cycle, all riding the flights layer's dead-reckoned entities. The FALSE FLAG side needs the simulated flights feed to speak the layer's expected shape — either register a new layer module against the DataLayerManager contract (id/init/enable/disable/update/getStats, earthquakes.js as the ~365-line template) or serve OpenSky /states-shaped JSON at the existing /api/opensky route (vite.config.js middleware seam, zero client changes). Aircraft and bases come from uk_forces in initial_conditions.yaml:83-294 (P-8s, E-7s, Typhoon squadrons at RAF_Lossiemouth/RAF_Coningsby, F-35Bs at RAF_Marham) so every ride-along is a real named unit the advisors also reference in prose. Patrol routes are authored splines between gazetteer points; the inject-flyby trick is just the ambient thread reading the upcoming episode's geo: block (idea 2) and biasing a route.
ideas.payoff: The 'wow' demo moment and the natural VR seed (a cockpit is the easiest XR frame: fixed seat, world moves); converts waiting time into exploration and builds player attachment to the same named assets their decisions later put at risk.

ideas.title: Home-front layer: domestic stability and media as visible life on the UK map
ideas.description: The war game's second front — panic buying, blackout at Drax, the Heathrow diplomatic exodus, media firestorms — currently exists only as prose and a 0-100 domestic_stability gauge. Render it: news-chyron markers and broadcast rings over cities when media injects land, city traffic/activity density that visibly thins as stability falls, and a simulated 'radio intercepts' layer voicing the intel desk's SIGINT prose at clickable points.
ideas.mechanism: Media-channel injects already route to the DOMESTIC layer via CHANNEL_LAYER_MAP (models/layers.py:37-53), so a globe client gets them pre-tagged with zero backend change; the gazetteer resolves their cities. Ambience density is driven by domestic_stability from state_update events, implemented on gods-eye-view's traffic.js precedent — the repo's proven, deterministic, keyless simulation mode (per-road-class speeds/densities over real OSM geometry) that already carries the honest 'SIMULATED' labeling convention the competition demo needs. The radio layer swaps Radio Garden points for in-fiction ones: engine/intelligence.py deterministically renders hidden metrics as SIGINT/media-monitoring prose on the INTEL layer today, and those lines become the 'transcript' behind clickable intercept markers at plausible locations, giving the hidden-metrics system a diegetic spatial voice.
ideas.payoff: Gives the neglected domestic axis equal dramatic weight with the naval picture — players report caring about stability when they can watch London dim — and reuses gods-eye-view's most complete built-in simulation verbatim rather than writing a new one.

ideas.title: Watch Officer voice brief: narrated globe tour opening every turn
ideas.description: Each briefing opens as a 30-second narrated GEOINT tour: a synthetic watch-officer voice summarizes the night's developments while the camera executes an authored recipe pass over each event location — orbital pullback, dive to the Orkney contact, sweep along the fleet's projected track — ending on the COBRA briefing screen. The player starts every turn oriented, in-fiction, without reading a wall of text.
ideas.mechanism: The engine already maintains the script's source: the rolling situation_summary and the turn's briefing inject. A prompt for the existing narrator LLMContext (llm/model_config.py:11-24), hot-editable via PUT /prompts/{family} (api/control.py:22-263), reformats them into a spoken watch brief with an ordered location list. The globe converts that list into a SceneDirector project — SCENE_RECIPES (src/scenes/recipes.js) like orbital-watch and omniscience-pullback are the authoring format — and plays it synced to TTS. Voice avoids the OpenAI dependency two ways: browser speechSynthesis for a $0 baseline, or Gemini live audio to stay on the game's single provider (the OpenAI Realtime stack in src/voice/ is cleanly severable — one optional initGevVoiceCommands call site — while gevActions.js remains an LLM-agnostic plain-JS action surface if two-way voice control is ever wanted). Cost-safe demo path: the deterministic dashboard_pack.json / WARGAME_LLM=mock capture replays a full narrated campaign with zero LLM spend, honoring the owner's 'money is real' rule.
ideas.payoff: Solves briefing-fatigue (the sim's densest reading moment) and produces the single most shareable competition artifact — a self-running narrated campaign replay is effectively a trailer that demonstrates the LLM, DTDL telemetry, and globe layers at once.

ideas.title: EXCON strike console: globe-originated injects with authored reveal cinematics
ideas.description: The facilitator's god-view globe becomes a two-way surface: click a point in the North Sea, and a pre-filled inject composer opens (nearest gazetteer name in the target field, channel, metric effects); on fire, the player's globe plays the corresponding reveal cinematic. Human exercise control gets the same dramatic vocabulary as scripted content — point at the world, make something happen there.
ideas.mechanism: The mutation seam is fully built: POST /game/{session_id}/inject (api/control.py:127-208, 403 unless facilitator=true) drives GameManager.deliver_inject (engine/game_manager.py:260-315), which reuses scripted-inject primitives, syncs hidden_metrics correctly (avoiding the documented silent-revert trap at engine/game_manager.py:296-307), and deliberately skips the event ledger. ManualInjectRequest's free-text 'target' field (api/control.py:136-138) is the existing stub to carry the clicked location's gazetteer name; the fired event already reaches players as a channel-layered transcript event plus a REFEREE 'inject_fired' record for the EXCON log. Cinematic authoring uses SceneDirector.captureShot/exportProject (src/scenes/director.js): the facilitator frames the shot on their own globe, and the captured JSON rides the inject so the player client plays it on receipt — the same reveal pipeline as idea 2, human-authored live. The globe page itself follows the proven zero-build pattern (api/dashboard.html served by FastAPI FileResponse), reusing its session-attach header and connectStream SSE wiring nearly verbatim and sidestepping the unbuildable Next.js frontend and the localhost-only CORS list.
ideas.payoff: Turns FALSE FLAG's facilitated-wargame heritage (the EXCON/REFEREE design in Game_Mechanics/War_Game_Mechanics.md) into a live performance instrument — a facilitator can improvise theatrically during a demo — and it exercises the DTDL/facilitator plumbing PRs #65/#66 just merged, making the competition story cohere.

ideas.title: Click-the-Globe Inject Console (geospatial EXCON)
ideas.description: Facilitator clicks any point on the Cesium globe; the client reverse-looks-up the nearest gazetteer entry (Faslane, Orkney_Islands, GIUK_gap...), opens a pre-filled inject composer (headline/channel/effects/severity), and fires it into the live session. The inject appears simultaneously in the player's transcript and as a georeferenced marker/camera fly-to on the globe, colored by its data-layer. This turns the existing invisible EXCON seam into the signature facilitator feature: spatial exercise control.
ideas.mechanism: POST /game/{session_id}/inject (api/control.py:141-208, fire_manual_inject) already accepts headline/content/channel/effects/target free-text and calls GameManager.deliver_inject (engine/game_manager.py:260-315) under session.lock with correct hidden-metrics sync — the 403 facilitator gate (api/control.py:157-161) is exactly right for this console. The globe client encodes the clicked place into the existing free-text 'target' field (api/control.py:136-138) as 'PLACE_NAME @lat,lon', and the server's 'inject_fired' REFEREE event plus the 'transcript' event (manual:true) echo it back over SSE so every attached screen renders the marker. Channel-to-layer coloring comes free from CHANNEL_LAYER_MAP (models/layers.py:37-53). The gazetteer is a new static JSON of the ~15 named locations in data/scenarios/war_game_2025/initial_conditions.yaml:305-323 plus base coordinates. Zero engine changes; the console page follows the zero-build api/dashboard.html FileResponse pattern (dtdl-merged api/server.py:1253) with Cesium from CDN.
ideas.payoff: Highest-visibility facilitator feature for the competition demo: 'drop a Kilo-class off Orkney by clicking Orkney' is a 10-second wow that exercises real game mechanics (metric effects, advisor awareness via recent_injects) through an endpoint that already exists — the whole build is client-side plus a gazetteer file.

ideas.title: Globe After-Action Replay from the DTDL Run Export
ideas.description: A replay page loads a completed run's DTDL Session instance and plays the entire campaign back on the globe: a Cesium clock scrubs T+0..T+n turn stamps, each inject_triggered fires a camera fly-to over its location, metric telemetry drives a globe-wide escalation glow, advisor_trust and phase_changed render as a HUD timeline, and the facilitator can pause on any turn to discuss the decision made there. Works entirely offline from the export — no live session, no LLM spend.
ideas.mechanism: The dtmi:falseflag:emergent:Session;1 export (interop/export_run.py build_run_document, sample at interop/sample_export/run_telemetry.json) already contains everything a replay needs, turn-indexed: 5 metric streams with turn-0 baselines, inject_triggered {turn, injectId, title, channel}, participant_action {turn, actionType, text}, phase_changed (4 points/turn), advisor_trust (per advisor per turn), plus decisions[] (AdjudicatedDecision with playerDecisionText/interpretation/effects/pushback) and ledger[] (EventLedgerEntry with disposition open|advanced|resolved). GET /dtdl/{dtmi} (dtdl-merged api/server.py:1229-1250) serves real instances at runtime. Location per inject comes from mapping injectId -> episode YAML -> gazetteer (scripted turns name real places in prose; the optional geo: block from the episode-authoring idea makes this exact). Camera choreography reuses gods-eye-view's SceneDirector JSON shot format (src/scenes/director.js: {camera:{lat,lon,alt,heading,pitch,roll}, durationSec, holdSec, visual:{style}}) — generate one scene per turn from the export. The deterministic mock pack (interop/demo_data/dashboard_pack.json, seed 42) is a free test fixture.
ideas.payoff: Converts the DTDL work from a compliance artifact into the AAR debrief product — the core serious-game deliverable ('what happened, where, and why') — and gives the AI Challenge judges a self-contained replayable demo that costs zero tokens and cannot fail live.

ideas.title: SSE Fan-Out plus Facilitator God-View (REFEREE ground truth on the globe)
ideas.description: Fix the single-consumer event queue so multiple screens can watch one session, then build the facilitator's god-view globe: it attaches with facilitator=true and therefore receives the REFEREE layer — raw adjudication effects before narrative dressing, inject_fired records, llm_call telemetry, parse_health — rendered as an omniscient overlay (true metric deltas floating over the map, red-force ground truth track, Mystery Mode antagonist highlighting) that player screens can never see.
ideas.mechanism: Prerequisite: GameSession's one asyncio.Queue (api/server.py:48-111) is destructively consumed by GET /stream, so two clients steal each other's events — replace with per-subscriber queues fanned out in push_event (a contained change in one class; _make_item stamping at api/server.py:78-97 is unchanged). The god-view is then free: _stream_filter (api/server.py:823-833) already drops REFEREE only for non-facilitator sessions, and the facilitator flag is fixed at POST /game/new (api/server.py:445-466), so hidden-truth separation is enforced server-side, not by client honesty. Red ground truth is synthesized from red_forces in initial_conditions.yaml:268-296 (15 vessels, location North_Atlantic_rendezvous, heading southwest_toward_UK) animated along the GIUK track using gods-eye-view's dead-reckoning pattern (flights.js interpolation between fixes). The 'adjudication' REFEREE event (api/server.py:160-228) carries raw effects/pushback/critical_concerns for the omniscient HUD.
ideas.payoff: Fan-out is the single enabler every multi-screen idea depends on (ops-room, spectator, replay late-join), and the god-view demonstrates the exercise-control story judges recognize from real wargaming: EXCON sees the truth, training audience sees the fog — enforced by an existing server-side filter, not UI convention.

ideas.title: Multi-Screen Ops-Room Mode (one screen per data layer)
ideas.description: A facilitator launches an ops-room configuration where each physical screen renders one of the six data layers around a central globe wall: SITREP main map, INTEL desk (assessment pulls), DIPLOMATIC board (per-country cables and calls), DOMESTIC media ticker, CABINET transcript wall, and the facilitator's REFEREE console. Screens are dumb SSE consumers of the same session, each filtering by the layer tag every event already carries — turning the single-player game into a staffed team exercise where different roles watch different feeds.
ideas.mechanism: Every event is stamped with layer/turn/t_plus_s/event_seq at the bus choke point GameSession._make_item (api/server.py:78-97), and the layer value travels inside the JSON payload, so a screen page filters with one if-statement — no server routing needed beyond the fan-out prerequisite. The six-layer vocabulary and colors already exist (models/layers.py Layer enum; dashboard.html legend chips --sitrep #4da3ff through --referee #ff5d5d). Each screen is a self-contained HTML page served via the proven FileResponse pattern (GET /dashboard, /dataflow — dtdl-merged api/server.py:1119,1253), parameterized by ?session_id=&layer=. Late-joining screens catch up via GET /game/{session_id} (transcript + active_call, api/server.py:525-543) and /game/{id}/state, /resources, /intel for initial scene state. The mandatory-call 409 gate (api/server.py:1010-1024) gives the DIPLOMATIC screen a natural dramatic beat: the turn-6 US call blocks all decisions until answered on that screen.
ideas.payoff: Re-frames FALSE FLAG from solo game to facilitated seminar wargame (the taxonomy Game_Mechanics/War_Game_Mechanics.md:10 explicitly draws on) with near-zero new server logic — the layer architecture was built for exactly this and has never been cashed in; it is also the physical-room demo that photographs best for a competition.

ideas.title: Assessment Overlay: Bloom-Level Objectives Scored Against Adjudicated Decisions
ideas.description: A facilitator-only overlay that projects pedagogical assessment onto the run: each turn's decision appears on the globe/timeline as a marker colored by its qualityVerdict (exceptional..catastrophic), flagged when the player overrode advisor objections, and cross-referenced against the exercise's LearningObjectives (Bloom taxonomy level, assessment criteria). At debrief, the facilitator walks the map turn by turn showing where good and catastrophic decisions were made and which objectives were evidenced.
ideas.mechanism: Both sides of the join already exist in the DTDL layer: dtmi:falseflag:LearningObjective;1 (exercise.json:109) carries statement/taxonomyLevel (Bloom remember..create)/assessmentMethod/assessmentCriteria[]/roles[], and dtmi:falseflag:emergent:AdjudicatedDecision;1 (emergent_assessment.json:4) carries turn/playerDecisionText/interpretation/qualityVerdict enum/reasoning/effects/pushback[]/criticalConcerns[]/overriddenObjectors[]. The Exercise->LearningObjective relationship and Session->decisions relationship are in the sample exports (exercise_war_game_2025.json, run_telemetry.json), so the overlay is a pure client join over GET /dtdl/{dtmi} instances — no engine or model changes. Quality verdicts are already regex-mined from adjudication replies in the capture path (export_run.py:63-79). Geoplacement reuses the replay gazetteer mapping (inject-of-turn -> place). overriddenObjectors[] renders as a warning glyph; EventLedgerEntry;1 dispositions (open|advanced|resolved) give a per-thread 'did the player close this out' column.
ideas.payoff: The cheapest idea on the list and the strongest serious-game credential: it demonstrates that the DTDL model was designed for assessment (objectives, taxonomy, verdicts) and delivers the measurable-training-value story an AI Challenge jury will ask about, using only data the export already emits.

ideas.title: Spectator Attract Mode: Self-Playing Campaign on the Globe
ideas.description: A booth/audience mode: one click starts a self-driving campaign whose events choreograph the globe cinematically — flash_alert injects trigger alarm-red camera dives, diplomatic events draw capital-to-capital arcs, escalation_risk drives global visual tension, and sensor modes (CRT/NVG/FLIR) crossfade per scene. Runs unattended for hours at the competition stand, with a QR code letting spectators open the player transcript on their phones.
ideas.mechanism: POST /demo/start (api/demo.py:69-167) already creates a facilitator session and a daemon thread that plays a full campaign (briefing -> mandatory-call answer -> cabinet question -> interpret+commit) at configurable pace_s, pushing every beat through the same tagged SSE bus and returning {session_id, stream}; with WARGAME_LLM=mock it is deterministic and free. The spectator globe subscribes to that stream and keys choreography off fields that already exist: inject channel -> treatment (flash_alert/emergency -> alert fly-to; diplomatic -> arc between capitals from WorldReference.organisations' 9 country actors), state_update metrics (api/server.py:214-218) -> escalation glow and simulated-traffic density, 'ending' events -> finale sequence. Camera language ports from gods-eye-view's SCENE_RECIPES format (src/scenes/recipes.js) and the six PostProcessStage GLSL styles (src/styles/thermal.js etc.), which are self-contained and drop into any Cesium viewer; theme-retro's phosphor green (frontend/app/globals.css) doubles as the NVG palette so the globe stays in the project's CRT register.
ideas.payoff: A zero-cost, cannot-fail exhibition demo (deterministic mock, no keys, no live data) that shows the whole system — engine, bus, layers, globe — running end-to-end without an operator; it is also the regression harness for every other globe feature since it replays identically every run.

ideas.title: Event Journal and Mid-Exercise Timeline Scrubber
ideas.description: Persist every stamped bus event to a per-session append-only journal and add a catch-up endpoint, then give the facilitator a timeline scrubber: drag back to any point in the run mid-exercise, see exactly what players had been told by then (per layer), jump the globe camera to any past inject, and resume live. Also fixes late-joining ops-room screens and observer devices, which currently see nothing that happened before they attached.
ideas.mechanism: Events already carry everything a journal needs — layer, turn, t_plus_s, event_seq stamped at the single choke point GameSession._make_item (api/server.py:78-97) — but sessions are an in-memory dict with no stream persistence (api/server.py:114) and Last-Event-ID is ignored, so replay is impossible today. The change is contained: append each stamped item to a per-session list (or JSONL file) inside _make_item, and add GET /game/{session_id}/events?since_seq=N&layer=... that respects the same REFEREE filter as _stream_filter (api/server.py:823-833). The scrubber UI is a pure client over that endpoint: event_seq gives total order, t_plus_s gives the time axis, turn gives chapter marks. The journal doubles as the live-session source for the DTDL export path (export_run.py build_run_document currently only works from batch capture), closing the gap between live play and the after-action replay artifact.
ideas.payoff: The smallest server change with the widest downstream unlock: late-join for every observer surface, mid-exercise 'what did we know and when' facilitation (a core real-world AAR question), and a bridge from live sessions to the DTDL replay/assessment products — currently only mock-captured runs can be replayed.

ideas.title: Geo-Authored Episodes: Optional geo Blocks in Turn YAML plus Pre-Brief Scenario Map
ideas.description: Extend episode authoring with an optional, engine-ignored geo: block per inject (entities, tracks, camera hints, place names with coordinates), and build the facilitator's pre-brief map: before the exercise, the whole scripted campaign renders as a spatial storyboard — where each of turns 1-6 will land, the Northern Fleet's authored track, which bases are implicated — so facilitators can brief observers and plan manual injects around the authored arc. During play the same blocks drive exact globe placement instead of prose guessing.
ideas.mechanism: Episode YAML dicts pass through load_inject_for_turn unvalidated — engine/events.py:43-81 returns the raw dict and the engine ignores unknown keys — so adding geo: {anchors:[{name, lat, lon}], track:{from,to,progress}, camera:{...}} to data/scenarios/war_game_2025/episodes/turn_NNN.yaml is fully backward-compatible with the engine, saves, and the difficulty-scaled effects pipeline (engine/sim_loop.py:188-295). The briefing_events mapper (api/server.py:141-157) — the declared single source of event shape for both the async endpoints and the demo thread — forwards the block onto the bus in one place. The pre-brief map needs no session at all: it parses episodes/*.yaml plus initial_conditions.yaml (locations block :305-323, red_forces track :268-296) directly. Rich targets already exist in prose ('12 nm off Orkney' turn_002, Drax turn_003, RAF Fylingdales turn_005) — authoring their coordinates is an afternoon of scenario work, not code. LLM-generated injects from turn 7 (llm/inject_generator.py) simply lack the block and fall back to gazetteer/no-placement, so parse risk is zero.
ideas.payoff: Establishes authored ground truth as the geo source (sidestepping the prose-vs-globe contradiction risk entirely for the scripted campaign that any competition demo will use), gives facilitators a genuine exercise-design artifact, and creates the schema precedent a future dtmi:falseflag:geo interface can formalize.

ideas.title: Ambient World Ticker: LLM GEOINT simulator streaming twin telemetry between turns
ideas.description: A background 'world simulator' agent that wakes when the engine goes quiescent (after resolve_decision, before the next POST /briefing) and scripts the next N minutes of ambient GEOINT: red-fleet vessels steaming the North_Atlantic -> GIUK_gap -> UK_waters track, QRA Typhoon sorties from RAF Lossiemouth/Coningsby, P-8 orbits, satellite passes. It streams continuous position fixes as new stream-only events, so the gods-eye-view globe is alive and animated exactly during the multi-minute LLM adjudication gaps when FALSE FLAG's engine runs nothing at all. This is the core 'between-inject/between-turn coordination layer' the owner wants, and it is only possible because FALSE FLAG has a sanctioned daemon-driver pattern plus a layer-tagged SSE bus, and gods-eye-view has a client that turns sparse fixes into smooth motion for free.
ideas.mechanism: Clone the api/demo.py daemon-thread pattern (bind api/llm_relay, sleep-paced outside GameSession.lock, mutate nothing under it): on each state_update event the ticker reads situation_summary + recent_injects + the ORBAT from GameManager.get_resources (engine/game_manager.py:1018-1129) and red_forces from data/scenarios/war_game_2025/initial_conditions.yaml:268-296, resolves place names through a ~20-entry gazetteer for the initial_conditions.yaml:305-323 named-locations block, then asks a new LLMContext (add e.g. GEO_AMBIENT to the 12-member enum in llm/model_config.py:11-24, prompt hot-editable via PUT /prompts/{family} in api/control.py) to emit a movement plan (entity, track waypoints, speed). The ticker interpolates fixes and pushes 'geo_track' events via GameSession.push_event_threadsafe (api/server.py:104) tagged with a new GEOINT value in the Layer enum (models/layers.py:16-25, ~5-line change; _stream_filter at api/server.py:823-833 passes any non-REFEREE layer to players automatically). Positions mirror into the dormant WorldState.spatial_state dict (models/world.py:40 — confirmed never read/written by the repo's own audit, and serialized in saves for free). Critically the ticker uses its own RNG and never calls deliver_inject or touches world.metrics, so the seeded-determinism invariant (engine/game_manager.py:860,936-940) and the hidden_metrics sync trap are untouched. On the globe side, either a new Cesium client consumes the SSE events directly, or the ticker's fixes are re-served in OpenSky /states/all JSON shape at gods-eye-view's /api/opensky and /api/aisstream vite-middleware seams (vite.config.js), so flights.js's 30s render-delay interpolation and constant-turn-rate dead reckoning animate them with zero client changes.
ideas.payoff: Turns FALSE FLAG's dead time (its defining weakness for a live demo — nothing executes between turns) into the product's signature feature: a continuously living operational picture that is provably decorative (stream-only, determinism preserved). Every other idea below consumes this feed.

ideas.title: Interrogate the globe: fog-of-war voice/text queries answered by the game LLM
ideas.description: Repurpose gods-eye-view's voice-AI pattern so a player asks the globe 'show me naval activity near the GIUK gap' and gets an in-fiction answer plus a camera response — but the answering brain is FALSE FLAG's own advisor_qa LLM, which structurally cannot leak hidden truth. The OpenAI Realtime plumbing is discarded; only the action grammar survives. This is a two-repo-only idea: gods-eye-view supplies a proven query->camera/layer action surface, FALSE FLAG supplies an in-fiction Q&A model whose knowledge is already permission-fenced.
ideas.mechanism: gods-eye-view's src/voice/gevActions.js is explicitly LLM-agnostic (camera verbs, layer toggles, SceneDirector calls as plain JS functions) and initGevVoiceCommands is a single severable call site (~5-6k lines of OpenAI code deleted cleanly per its own architecture). Replace the tool-dispatch half of gevRealtime.js with a call to POST /game/discussion (the advisor_qa family), packaging the contextStore.js/analystEngine.js scene snapshot (camera position, enabled layers, tracked entity) into the question. The reply text renders as an advisor transcript line AND drives gevActions: fly-to via gazetteer lookup, layer enables keyed to the answer's Layer tag. Fog-of-war is free by construction: player sessions never receive REFEREE events (_stream_filter, api/server.py:823-833), advisor_qa prompts never receive the Mystery-mode NarrativeConfig (models/narrative.py:44-150 routes secret motives only to actor_simulation/diplomacy), and the intel desk (engine/intelligence.py) already renders hidden metrics as confidence-graded SIGINT prose — so 'what is the Russian fleet doing?' returns an honest, in-fiction, uncertainty-laden assessment rather than ground truth. Voice in/out can be added later (Gemini Live audio, matching the project's existing Gemini stack per docs/GEMINI_SETUP.md) without changing the dispatch layer.
ideas.payoff: The single strongest judge-facing demo moment for the AI Challenge: natural-language interrogation of a photorealistic globe where the answer is generated by the game's cabinet AI under real epistemic constraints — a capability neither repo has alone and no off-the-shelf tool has at all.

ideas.title: dtmi:falseflag:geo:* — the DTDL twin graph as the single source for globe, dashboard, and Azure replay
ideas.description: Extend the just-validated 13-interface DTDL model with a GeoAsset interface and a geo_event telemetry stream, making one twin schema drive three surfaces simultaneously: the Cesium globe (live), the dashboard twin panel (live counts), and Azure Digital Twins / 3D Scenes Studio (post-hoc replay of an exported run). The globe client discovers its own data contract at runtime from GET /dtdl instead of hardcoding event names.
ideas.mechanism: Add interop/models/geo_asset.json — dtmi:falseflag:geo:GeoAsset;1 with Properties (name, kind enum vessel|submarine|aircraft|base|sensor, affiliation enum blue|red|neutral) and Telemetry position as a plain Object{lat:double, lon:double, alt:double, heading:double, speed:double, turn:int} (the ADT-safe encoding — DTDL geospatial schemas are Telemetry-only and unqueryable in ADT), plus a geo_event stream added to Session (as Session;2 or additive contents) and a GeoLocation;1 gazetteer twin per entry in initial_conditions.yaml:305-323 so Inject/EventLedgerEntry can reference places by relationship instead of free text (WorldReference;1's 'location' is currently a bare string — interop/models/world_reference.json:8). The GET /dtdl endpoint auto-serves anything dropped in interop/models/ (it globs the directory — dtdl-merged/api/server.py:1137-1181), so the globe binds entities to DTMIs with no registration step. Required plumbing, all identified: extend validate_dtdl.py's schema whitelist, update test_interop.py's hard-coded 'exactly 9 streams' assert (line 93-99), re-run Microsoft's DTDLParser to keep the official-parser-clean claim, and add a geo telemetry array to export_run.py's build_run_document (line 390) fed from the Ambient Ticker's recorded fixes so run_telemetry.json replays the whole spatial campaign in ADT. Versioned DTMIs make this purely additive for existing consumers.
ideas.payoff: The strongest standards story available to the competition entry: 'one DTDL model, parsed clean by Microsoft's official parser, drives the live XR globe, the facilitator dashboard, and an Azure Digital Twins replay' — a genuine interoperability claim, not demo glue, and it converts the PR #65/#66 work from documentation into load-bearing infrastructure.

ideas.title: Peacetime baseline + simulated crisis deltas, using the traffic.js honest-labeling pattern
ideas.description: Blend real live feeds and simulated fiction on one globe without misinformation risk, by generalizing the dual-mode pattern gods-eye-view already ships: fiction-neutral layers (USGS earthquakes, CelesTrak satellites, civil traffic) stay LIVE as ambient peacetime texture, while conflict-relevant layers (military flights, vessels in UK waters) come from the FALSE FLAG feed server and are labeled EXERCISE on every surface. Crisis deltas modulate the live baseline: as escalation_risk climbs, simulated NOTAMs thin civil air traffic over the North Atlantic and simulated AIS gaps appear near the fleet.
ideas.mechanism: gods-eye-view's traffic.js (~2,400 lines) is the in-repo precedent: it runs a full deterministic simulation whenever /api/tomtom/status returns hasKey:false and labels the layer 'SIMULATED — add TomTom key for live'; README codifies honest labeling as a design principle. Reuse that exact switch per layer: point the /api/opensky, /api/aisstream, /api/adsb.lol middleware routes (vite.config.js, the declared zero-client-change seam) at a FALSE FLAG scenario feed server emitting OpenSky/AIS-shaped JSON from the Ambient Ticker, and stamp every simulated layer's getRowControls() status chip and legend with EXERCISE labeling; leave /api/celestrak, /api/firms (earthquakes/USGS is keyless) live. The delta logic subscribes to state_update events ({phase, turn, metrics} — api/server.py:214-218): escalation_risk thresholds gate filter functions applied to the live feeds before they reach the client (e.g. suppress live tracks entering a declared exclusion zone and substitute simulated diversions), so reality is only ever subtracted-and-replaced, never silently altered. This also honors the reports' collision warning: real Oct-2026 peace under a fictional Oct-2025 war is only coherent if military layers are simulated by construction, which this split enforces.
ideas.payoff: Photorealistic ambient credibility (real satellites actually overhead, real seismicity) with a structurally-enforced fiction boundary — directly answers the 'misinformation optics in a competition demo' risk while making the crisis feel like a disturbance in a real world rather than a synthetic diorama.

ideas.title: Inject-to-cinematic: SceneDirector JSON generated per inject, keyed by channel-to-layer semantics
ideas.description: Every inject becomes a deterministic camera cutscene: a flash_alert flies the camera to Orkney under the thermal/FLIR shader with detection overlays; an intelligence inject pans Severomorsk in NVG surveillance mode; a media inject frames London through the retro/CRT filter — matching FALSE FLAG's codified CRT aesthetic (frontend CRTOverlay.tsx, theme-retro's phosphor green is already an NVG palette). Authored injects can carry hand-tuned shots; generated injects get shots synthesized from the gazetteer.
ideas.mechanism: gods-eye-view's SceneDirector (src/scenes/director.js, ~1,200 lines) is a JSON-serializable cutscene engine: scenes -> shots with camera {lat,lon,alt,heading,pitch,roll}, per-shot duration/hold, visual style + styleParams, and per-layer toggles, with importProjectFile/startScene as the programmatic entry (PROJECT_VERSION 3, SCENE_RECIPES in recipes.js as the authoring template). On the FALSE FLAG side, episode YAML passes through load_inject_for_turn unvalidated (engine/events.py:43-81 returns the raw dict), so an optional 'geo:' block (waypoints, camera hints, sensor mode) in turn_NNN.yaml files is backward-compatible today; the briefing_events mapper (api/server.py:141-157) forwards it on the inject's transcript event. Default shots are derived mechanically: CHANNEL_LAYER_MAP (models/layers.py:37-53) maps channel -> visual treatment, the gazetteer maps the inject's named places -> coordinates, and the six portable PostProcessStage GLSL modules (src/styles/thermal.js etc. — self-contained {name, uniforms, fragmentShader}, usable on any Cesium viewer) supply the sensor look. For stochastic turn-7+ injects, either extend the generator prompt (llm/prompts.py:454-468) with an optional locations list or run a GEO_EXTRACTION LLMContext over the prose. Both sides are deterministic (seeded engine; director token/AbortSignal cancellation), so the same save replays the same film.
ideas.payoff: The inject — FALSE FLAG's atomic dramatic unit, currently a wall of prose — becomes a broadcast-quality visual beat with zero engine changes, and the reuse story ('their cinematic director, our narrative engine') is legible to judges in one sentence.

ideas.title: CCTV and radio layers as explorable in-game media injects
ideas.description: Repurpose gods-eye-view's CCTV (~800 cameras) and Radio Garden layers into diegetic evidence surfaces: DOMESTIC-layer media injects spawn clickable 'camera' pins at their named locations (Drax power station, Scrabster ferry terminal, Heathrow) showing generated stills or ASCII-fog-treated freeze frames, and a SIGINT/radio layer plays the intel desk's monitoring product as geolocated intercept pins whose confidence grading is real game state. The player physically hunts the globe for the story instead of reading a feed.
ideas.mechanism: Both layers already fetch through replaceable middleware routes (/api/cctv, /api/radio in vite.config.js) and the layer contract is a plain object copyable from earthquakes.js (~365 lines, the minimal template) registered via dataManager.register() in main.js. The content pipeline is entirely in-repo: inject channel 'media' maps to Layer.DOMESTIC and 'intelligence' to INTEL via CHANNEL_LAYER_MAP (models/layers.py:37-53), so a globe layer subscribed to the SSE stream can spawn a pin per matching transcript event, geolocated by gazetteer lookup on the inject's place names (rich in prose: '12 nm off Orkney', MV Hamnavoe, RAF Fylingdales); FALSE FLAG's Graphics/ directory is an existing SDXL/ASCII asset pipeline for generating the stills, and injects already support an optional 'image' field in episode YAML (engine/events.py). For radio, engine/intelligence.py deterministically renders hidden metrics as SIGINT/cable-traffic/media-monitoring prose with confidence codes — exactly the content for intercept pins, delivered on the INTEL layer with its 'assessment_pulled' event ({actor, code, confidence} — already on the bus). The facilitator can also drop ad-hoc media via POST /game/{session_id}/inject (api/control.py:127-208), whose free-text 'target' field geolocates the pin.
ideas.payoff: Converts FALSE FLAG's richest untapped asset — location-dense inject prose — into spatial gameplay, and gives the 'between-turn coordination phase' a player verb (investigate, correlate, brief the cabinet on what you found) rather than passive watching.

ideas.title: Dual-view EXCON globe: REFEREE god-view in XR with globe-originated injects
ideas.description: Two globes from one event bus: the player's globe shows only the fog-of-war picture, while a facilitator XR view shows adversary ground truth (actual red tracks from the Ambient Ticker's REFEREE-tagged fixes, Mystery-mode antagonist state, raw adjudication effects) — and the facilitator authors injects by clicking the globe: pick a location, compose headline/effects, fire it into the live game. The gods-eye-view cockpit/tracking machinery gives the facilitator a literal periscope-view of any simulated entity.
ideas.mechanism: The permission fence already exists server-side: sessions created with facilitator=true (POST /game/new, api/server.py:445-466) receive the REFEREE layer; _stream_filter (api/server.py:823-833) strips it for everyone else — so the dual view is purely a matter of tagging ground-truth geo fixes REFEREE and fog-of-war fixes SITREP/INTEL at the Ambient Ticker. Facilitator REFEREE events already carry the payloads an EXCON display wants: 'adjudication' (raw effects/pushback), 'llm_call' (family/latency/model), 'inject_fired'. Inbound authoring uses the existing EXCON seam verbatim: POST /game/{session_id}/inject -> GameManager.deliver_inject (engine/game_manager.py:260-315), which applies metric effects with correct hidden_metrics sync and deliberately skips the event ledger; the ManualInjectRequest 'target' free-text field (api/control.py:136-138) is the designated stub to carry the clicked gazetteer name/coordinates. gods-eye-view contributes the god-view ergonomics: per-entity trackById/cockpitView (cockpitTracking.js) for riding a red submarine, and the layer-toggle sidebar pattern mapping 1:1 onto the six-layer legend the dashboard already renders. Prerequisite shared with all multi-client ideas: fan-out the single-consumer asyncio.Queue in GameSession (api/server.py:48-111) into per-subscriber queues, since today a second SSE client steals events from the first.
ideas.payoff: Reproduces the NATO EXCON/white-cell structure the game's own mechanics doc cites (Game_Mechanics/War_Game_Mechanics.md) as a live two-screen demo — judges watch the player's uncertain picture and the referee's truth diverge in real time, which is the entire epistemic thesis of FALSE FLAG made visible.

ideas.title: Zero-spend attract mode: demo driver + mock LLM + fictional clock driving the globe unattended
ideas.description: A one-command exhibition mode for the competition booth: POST /demo/start spins up a self-playing full campaign, the globe attaches to its stream, and a fictional clock slews Cesium time between turn timestamps so satellites propagate, the day/night terminator crawls, and vessels steam at plausible speeds — all with WARGAME_LLM=mock, i.e. deterministic and costing zero API spend, honoring the owner's 'money is real' rule.
ideas.mechanism: api/demo.py already runs an unattended campaign (briefing -> mandatory-call answer -> cabinet question -> interpret+commit) in a daemon thread at configurable pace_s, returning {session_id, stream:'/stream/{id}'} — a ready-made feed the globe consumes like any session; WARGAME_LLM=mock makes every turn instant and deterministic (seed default 42), and interop/demo_data/dashboard_pack.json plus export_run.py's capture path provide a canned recorded campaign as a no-server fallback. The fictional clock exploits a documented quirk: episode headers carry real fictional timestamps (turn 1 = Sun 5 Oct 2025 17:00, ~2-3h per turn) that the engine never mechanically advances (game_time set once — engine/game_manager.py:148-152), so the globe client is free to own time — it maps the between-turn wall-clock window onto the turn N -> N+1 fictional interval and drives viewer.clock accordingly, which gods-eye-view's satellites layer (SGP4 via satellite.js) and flights dead-reckoning respect natively. phase_changed telemetry (DTDL Session stream 8) and state_update events supply the slew/freeze triggers across discussion/decision phases; escalation_risk from the same events drives ambient intensity (sensor-noise, military-flight ratio) the way gods-eye-view layers already parameterize density. Pacing degrades gracefully in both directions: mock mode compresses turns to seconds (clock slews fast), real LLM mode stretches them to minutes (clock slews slow).
ideas.payoff: Solves the unglamorous problem that decides competition demos: something compelling must be running on the stand at all times, deterministically, without an operator or an API bill — and it doubles as the integration testbed every other idea here develops against.
